pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 하늘나라 임금님의 아들 환웅이 살았어요. 환웅은 구름 사이로 아래 세상을 가만히 내려다보았지요. 푸른 산과 들이 반짝반짝, 시냇물이 졸졸졸. "저 땅에 내려가 사람들과 함께 살고 싶구나."
pages.t: Long, long ago, up in the land of heaven, there lived Hwanung, the son of the King of Heaven. Hwanung looked down quietly through the clouds at the world below. The green hills and fields sparkled, and the little streams went trickle, trickle, trickle. "How I would love to go down to that land and live with the people there."

pages.ko: 환웅은 바람과 비와 구름을 데리고 스르륵— 산꼭대기 큰 나무 아래로 내려왔어요. 사람들은 그 나무를 신단수라고 불렀지요. 나무 옆에는 나무 새를 얹은 솟대를 높이높이 세웠어요. 환웅은 씨앗 뿌리는 법도, 아플 때 낫는 법도 하나하나 알려 주었답니다.
pages.t: Hwanung brought the wind and the rain and the clouds along with him, and down he came — whoosh! — to a great tree at the top of a mountain. The people called that tree Sindansu, the holy tree. Beside it they raised a tall wooden pole with a wooden bird on top, up, up, high in the air. Hwanung taught the people everything: how to plant seeds, and how to get well when they were sick.

pages.ko: 어느 날 곰 한 마리와 호랑이 한 마리가 어슬렁어슬렁 찾아왔어요. 마을에서는 둥둥— 북소리가 울리고 있었지요. "환웅님, 저희도 사람이 되고 싶어요!" 곰은 앞발을 가지런히 모으고, 호랑이는 꼬리를 팔랑팔랑 흔들었답니다.
pages.t: One day a bear and a tiger came padding along. In the village the drums were booming — boom, boom! "Hwanung, we want to be people too!" The bear folded her front paws neatly, and the tiger swished his tail back and forth.

pages.ko: 환웅은 빙그레 웃으며 쑥 한 다발과 마늘 스무 쪽을 내주었어요. "이것만 먹으면서, 백 날 동안 햇빛을 보지 말고 동굴에서 지내 보렴." 곰과 호랑이는 눈을 반짝 뜨고 고개를 끄덕끄덕했지요. "백 날쯤이야, 문제없어요!"
pages.t: Hwanung smiled and gave them a bundle of mugwort and twenty cloves of garlic. "Eat only this, and stay in a cave for one hundred days without seeing the sunlight." The bear and the tiger opened their eyes wide and nodded and nodded. "A hundred days? That's easy!"

pages.ko: 곰과 호랑이는 나란히 동굴로 들어갔어요. 입구로 들어온 햇빛 한 줌만 동그랗게 밝았지요. 둘은 마주 보고 놀이하듯 노래를 시작했어요. "쑥 한 입, 마늘 한 쪽, 하나 둘 셋! 오늘도 잘 참았다, 하나 둘 셋!"
pages.t: Side by side, the bear and the tiger went into the cave. Only one round handful of sunlight came in at the doorway. The two of them looked at each other and started up a song, as if it were a game. "One bite of mugwort, one clove of garlic, one two three! We waited well again today, one two three!"

pages.ko: 하루, 이틀, 열흘… 쑥은 쌉싸름하고 마늘은 알알했어요. 곰은 오물오물 천천히 씹었지만, 호랑이는 "우웩!" 하고 혀를 쏙 내밀었지요. "곰아, 넌 그게 어떻게 맛있니?" "맛있진 않아. 그냥 하나씩 세면 괜찮아."
pages.t: One day, two days, ten days… the mugwort was bitter and the garlic bit their tongues. The bear chewed slowly, munch munch, but the tiger stuck out his tongue and said, "Bleh!" "Bear, how can you like that?" "I don't like it. But if I just count them one by one, it's all right."

pages.ko: 스무 밤이 지나자 호랑이는 온몸이 근질근질했어요. 발끝이 들썩들썩, 꼬리가 씰룩씰룩. "나는 달리고 싶어! 바람도 쐬고 싶어! 폴짝 뛰고 싶어!" 호랑이는 그만 벌떡 일어서고 말았답니다.
pages.t: After twenty nights the tiger was itchy all over. His toes wiggled and his tail twitched. "I want to run! I want to feel the wind! I want to jump high!" And up the tiger sprang, right onto his feet.

pages.ko: 호랑이는 동굴 밖으로 훌쩍 뛰어나갔어요. 환한 빛 속에서 후련하게 크게 숨을 쉬었지요. 곰은 하나도 화내지 않고 손을 흔들어 주었어요. "잘 가, 호랑이야. 달리는 건 네가 제일 잘하잖아!"
pages.t: Out of the cave the tiger leaped. In the bright light he took a big, happy breath. The bear was not one bit angry — she waved her paw goodbye. "Bye, Tiger. Running is the thing you do best of all!"

pages.ko: 이제 동굴에는 곰 혼자였어요. 곰은 하루가 지날 때마다 벽에 금을 하나씩 쓱— 그었어요. 심심하면 혼자서 노래를 불렀지요. "쑥 한 입, 마늘 한 쪽, 하나 둘 셋! 오늘도 잘 참았다, 하나 둘 셋!"
pages.t: Now the bear was all alone in the cave. Every time a day went by, she scratched one line on the wall. And when she felt lonely, she sang her song all by herself. "One bite of mugwort, one clove of garlic, one two three! We waited well again today, one two three!"

pages.ko: 드디어 백 번째 금을 긋던 날! "아흔여덟, 아흔아홉, 백! 다 참았다, 하나 둘 셋!" 동굴 안이 환해지더니 곰의 몸이 스르르 빛에 감싸였어요. 눈을 떠 보니— 곰은 어여쁜 여인이 되어 있었지요. 사람들은 그를 웅녀라고 불렀답니다.
pages.t: At last came the day of the hundredth line! "Ninety-eight, ninety-nine, one hundred! I waited all the way, one two three!" The cave grew bright, and light wrapped softly all around the bear. When she opened her eyes — the bear had become a lovely woman! The people called her Ungnyeo.

pages.ko: 환웅과 웅녀는 부부가 되었어요. 얼마 뒤, 볼이 통통한 사내아이가 태어났지요. 이름은 단군! 마을 사람들은 제기에 햇곡식을 소복이 담아 하늘에 감사드리고, 북을 둥둥 울리며 덩실덩실 춤을 추었답니다.
pages.t: Hwanung and Ungnyeo were married. Not long after, a baby boy with round, chubby cheeks was born. His name was Dangun! The village people piled the new grain high on their special dishes to thank the heavens, and they beat the drums — boom, boom! — and danced and danced.

pages.ko: 아기 단군은 무럭무럭 자랄 거예요. 언젠가 이 넓고 넓은 땅에 우리나라를 세운대요. 솟대 위 나무 새가 훨훨— 하늘을 가리켰지요. 그날 산에서 내려온 호랑이도 "어흥!" 하고 반갑게 축하해 주었답니다. 참는 것도, 달리는 것도 저마다의 멋진 재주예요. 꾹 참고 기다린 마음은 언젠가 꼭 환하게 피어난대요.
pages.t: Baby Dangun would grow up big and strong. One day, they say, he would build our country on this wide, wide land. On top of the tall pole, the wooden bird pointed its wings up at the sky. And that day the tiger came down from the mountain too, and roared "Grrraowr!" to say congratulations. Waiting is a wonderful gift, and so is running — everyone has their own. And a heart that waits patiently will bloom bright and beautiful someday.
